_README: Every callback seam that is CALLED through a NULL check and filled by
nobody needs a row here. tools/seam_audit.py measures the set; the
source-tools test refuses a seam that is empty and unledgered, and also
a row here for a seam that is no longer empty -- so a wiring cannot
leave a stale excuse behind, and a new empty seam cannot appear
The point is not that every seam must be wired. Plenty stand for
drawing this port has no renderer for. The point is that leaving one
empty has to be a decision somebody wrote down, because an unwired seam
is invisible: the call compiles, runs, does nothing, and reads exactly
like working code. Six separate findings this cycle were that shape.
display   - object/DMA drawing; this port has no renderer
hardware  - talks to the cabinet (CMOS clock, DIPs, I/O)
fallback  - the call sites run the real routine in an else
unreached - the caller itself is not on a live path
deferred  - real, wireable, and not yet done; the note says what is
known and what still has to be established

show_title.note: ATTRACT.ASM SHOW_TITLE's title screen. The attract sequence's decisions -- which screen, in what order, for how long -- are translated and tested (wm/attract.h, src/generated/attract_sequence.c); what each screen PAINTS is not, and src/generated/port_status.c already reports it as not-started. Filling this seam would need a renderer, not a translation.

read_clock.note: The CMOS real-time clock the time-and-date screen reads. There is no clock chip here, and inventing a time would make the screen lie.

time_date_dip_enabled.note: The operator DIP that enables the time-and-date screen. No switch bank to read; the screen it gates is display anyway.

remap_io.note: REMAP_IO, the cabinet's I/O address window, which the attract path reopens around the screens that touch hardware directly. There is no memory-mapped I/O window on this machine to remap, so the call has nothing to stand for.

music_adjustment_nonzero.note: The operator's music volume adjustment, read out of CMOS by the attract adapter to decide whether to play music at all. No adjustment store and no CMOS here; a default would be the cabinet's setting invented rather than read.

pal_getf.note: pal_getf, a palette allocation. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

screen_flash.note: the full-screen flash. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

shadow_trail.note: the shadow trail a moving object leaves. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

impact.note: the impact sprite a landed blow spawns. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

flash_white.note: flash_white's QDMAN fill of the whole screen. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

restore_hit_render_state.note: putting the palette back after a hit flash. Object, palette or DMA work with no renderer behind it. The decision that reaches it is translated; the drawing is not.

keep_attached.note: WRESTLE.ASM keep_attached. Not a hole: every call site reads `if (c && c->keep_attached) ... else (void)wm_arcade_keep_attached(a);`, so the real translated routine runs when the seam is empty. All seven shared dispatchers were checked. The seam exists so a backend CAN take it over, not because anything is missing.

auto_pin_check.note: A field of wm_arcade_move_wrestler's callback set (wm/arcade/wm_arcade_move_dispatch.h). That routine is the FAITHFUL translation of WRESTLE.ASM's move_wrestler and is called only from a test; the live loop calls wm_arcade_move_ported_wrestler, its last step alone. Why the split exists and what it would take to collapse it -- deciding whether SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR carries an id or an address for everybody -- is recorded under `auto_pin` in port/translation_manifest.json. auto_pin_check itself IS translated and IS called live, from match.c, where the source calls it.

resolve_label_token.note: With start_special_label, the two halves of the six shared dispatchers' startsp(): resolve the animation label to a token for SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR, then start it. Both empty, so startsp() is inert end to end. NOT yet established whether that matters: the live special-move path is match_tick_smoves_for, which starts the animation itself, and for seven of the eight wrestlers SPECIAL_MOVE_ADDR is vestigial (see `auto_pin`). Tracing whether any startsp() call site is reachable other than through the monitors is the work; until that is done, wiring it would be guessing at which of two paths is the real one.

attacker_anim_tag.note: REACT1.ASM hit_stomp compares the attacker's current ANIBASE label against specific ones. The seam resolves that comparison for the reaction core; empty, hit_stomp reads WM_R_ANIMTAG_OTHER for everybody and takes the general arm. Real and wireable -- the label is on the backend -- but which labels map to which tag has to be read off REACT1.ASM rather than assumed.

move_grade.note: REACT's per-move grading, which feeds the award and message paths. The grades themselves are computed; this seam only reports them, so nothing downstream currently hears. Wireable once there is a consumer that is not display.

unhandled_reaction.note: The reaction core's own escape hatch for a hit_table entry it has no handler for -- diagnostic rather than behaviour. Worth filling with a counter so the number is measured instead of assumed, which is its own small change.

attacker_uses_lex_flykick_anim.note: One REACT1 special case that asks whether the attacker is playing Lex's flying-kick animation. A label comparison like attacker_anim_tag's and blocked on the same reading.

ck_ignore_reversed.note: Razor's twin of ck_ignore, taking BOTH wrestlers rather than one. ck_ignore is wired now against wm_arcade_ck_ignore; this one's source routine and its second argument have not been identified yet, and pointing it at the one-argument translation would be inventing the difference away.

bonus_message.note: The bonus text a special move puts on screen, plus the award behind it. The message is display; whether an award rides along -- as it does in DO_REVERSAL_MESS, which is why that one got wired -- has to be read off the callers.

first_hit_message.note: The FIRST HIT banner. Its AWARD half is already wired separately through react_cb.round_first_hit_award (ANIM.ASM:2253's `RND_AWARD a13,FIRST_HIT_AWD`), so what is left behind this seam is the drawing.

partner_breakout.note: A teammate breaking up a hold in buddy mode. The port runs a fixed pair by default; the call site is live only with four actors, and the routine behind it has not been traced.

round_award_block.note: AWARD.ASM's block award. The award machinery is all here (wm_award_round_award, and BLOCK is an index in wm/award.h); what is missing is reading which block events the source scores, which is not the same question as how to score them.

jump_rope_audio.note: Bret's jump-rope taunt audio. A WRSND like the ones wired this cycle, but its move mnemonic has not been read off BRET.ASM yet.

start_shake.note: The Undertaker's coffin finish asking for a screen shake. wm_shake_start is translated and is wired for REACT4 already, so this is a short wiring -- it wants the finish sequence's own test rather than riding along with an unrelated change.

play_wrestler_tune.note: DO_RIGHT_MUSIC's per-wrestler victory tune, which the attract adapter asks for by wrestler number. wm_match_wrestler_tune already resolves WHICH tune (it is asserted in wm_test_match_end), so what is missing behind this seam is playing it -- the DCS tune path, which is the same cluster as do_tune_commands and snd_update and wants one pass of its own rather than a single call bolted on.
